intro: Cement masons coordinate crews, check quality and work fast before concrete sets. The closest of the 25 careers below is helping brick, stone and tile setters at an 85% match, but rail and mining jobs pay more, such as Locomotive Engineers at a BLS May 2025 median of $81,410, or 43% more.
why_it_works: Finishing concrete means reading the mix and the weather, timing each step and getting a smooth, level surface on the first try. O*NET rates coordination, time management and quality control at 3.12 out of 5 for this job. Welding, refractory repair and rail work use the same hands-on skills. All 25 matches need no extra schooling. The gaps are maintenance and repair work.
tips: Railroads hire from the trades: rail-track equipment operators earn $70,070, which is 23% more.
Refractory Materials Repairers earn $61,290, or 7% more, and use your masonry skills in plants.
A welding certificate opens a large trade with steady demand across many industries.

faq.q: What jobs can former cement masons do?
faq.a: The closest matches are helpers for brick, stone and tile setters (85%), surface mining excavating operators (75%) and refractory materials repairers (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Welders are also 75% matched and earn $53,750, which is 6% less than the $57,020 cement mason median.

faq.q: Which careers for cement masons pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more. Locomotive Engineers earn $81,410 (43% more), rail-track equipment operators $70,070 (23% more) and railroad brake and signal operators $68,840 (21% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Railroads train new workers on the job.

faq.q: Do cement masons need more education to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than cement masons and concrete finishers already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 58% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, so apprenticeships and certificates matter more than degrees.

faq.q: What skills should cement masons learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, equipment maintenance, operations monitoring and repairing. Complex problem solving already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning to run and fix equipment is the main step toward better-paid trades.
